It also supports multilingual service and is positioned to improve the shopping and payments experience for Klarna customers worldwide.

Klarna has also added chat-based shopping features to its assistant.

answer.what_it_does: Klarna's AI assistant is an OpenAI-powered customer service agent built into the Klarna app and web experience, launched in February 2024, that answers consumer questions and handles tasks such as refunds, returns, payment issues and order status in more than 35 languages. Klarna says customers can still choose to reach live human agents, and the assistant hands complex cases to people.

incidents_or_risks.what: Customers complained the AI gave generic answers and could not handle complicated or nuanced questions; Klarna had also let go of customer service staff with institutional knowledge. Klarna responded that it saw no drop in consumer satisfaction.

CEO Sebastian Siemiatkowski said cost had been too dominant an evaluation factor in organizing support, which produced lower quality, and Klarna began rehiring human agents and promised customers a human option.

Klarna's public Q3 2025 update said the assistant does the work of 853 agents, versus the earlier 700 figure, with roughly $60M in annual savings. Critics said the 700 framing was misleading because it described avoided hiring during growth rather than layoffs.

Third-party analysis reported that the assistant sometimes gave confident but wrong answers about policy, fees or payment terms on edge cases, which the author treats as a compliance problem in fintech. This is an analyst's assessment, not a Klarna disclosure.
Secondhand reporting of a hands-on critique found the assistant mainly automates Level-1 support and documented prompt-injection vulnerabilities alongside the guardrails Klarna deployed.

incidents_or_risks.what: A reported concern that AI handling disputes and account closures autonomously raised compliance questions, and that customer satisfaction dropped on complex or emotional tickets even when answers were correct (third-party summary).

facts.claim: Klarna announced the AI assistant on February 27, 2024; in its first month it handled 2.3 million conversations, about two-thirds of Klarna's customer service chats, which Klarna said equaled the work of 700 full-time agents.
Klarna said the assistant was available in 23 markets, around the clock, in more than 35 languages, and that customer satisfaction was on par with human agents.
Klarna reported average resolution time fell from 11 minutes to under 2 minutes and repeat inquiries dropped 25%.
Klarna's Q3 2025 public update put the assistant at the work of 853 agents and about $60M in annual savings.
In a May 2025 statement, Klarna said it was 'not reversing on AI' and that its AI assistant performed the work of over 800 full-time roles.

Klarna's assistant is described as agentic: it accesses customer data, tracks ticket state, issues returns and manages payment plans, with a 100-person specialist team added to support complex queries alongside outsourced agents.
Klarna's human support is now described as a freelance, on-demand model paying agents per shift, with AI kept in the loop for routine queries.
Klarna's outsourced external human agent count reportedly fell from about 3,000 to 2,300 as AI took on routine work.

Klarna's assistant was built on OpenAI's GPT-4-class models, with integrations to Klarna's account and transaction systems and a help-center knowledge base (per third-party analysis, not confirmed by Klarna).
